author: golden state today
title: UC Irvine's Paul Merage School of Business reduces MBA tuition
text:
The Paul Merage School of Business at the University of California, Irvine announced on May 6 that it will reduce tuition for its Flex MBA and Executive MBA programs by up to 38 percent and introduce a redesigned curriculum with artificial intelligence integration.
This move aims to make graduate business education more accessible for working professionals. The school said the Flex MBA tuition will decrease by $30,000 and the Executive MBA tuition by $48,000. With the new price of $99,000 for the Flex MBA, students can now finance their degree entirely within federal loan limits.
“This is about access and relevance,” said Ian O. Williamson, dean of the Merage School of Business. “We’ve redesigned these programs to reflect today’s economy, where AI, flexibility and return on investment matter, and made them more attainable for professionals ready to advance their career. A University of California MBA, now priced below the federal loan cap. That combination simply didn’t exist in this market before today.”
The updated programs include expanded flexible learning options, shorter time to completion and an AI-infused curriculum designed to build practical skills valued in today’s job market. “We believe these programs now represent the best value MBA in California: a world-class, highly ranked degree at a price point that is accessible and viable for working professionals across all communities,” Williamson said.
The university reports that its campus is home to over 36,000 students and offers 224 degree programs while being Orange County’s second-largest employer according to the official website . UC Irvine participates in NCAA Division I athletics as the Anteaters; it holds very high research activity status under Carnegie classification; operates within the University of California system; emphasizes inclusive excellence through research collaborations; engages internationally; and maintains accreditation from the Western Association of Schools and Colleges Senior College and University Commission according to the official website .
For more information about program details or application procedures at UC Irvine’s Paul Merage School of Business or other offerings at UC Irvine visit https://merage.uci.edu/tuition-reduction .
